primitives.name: Heterogeneous Treatment Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research question Do software patches (game-balance interventions) affect players and teams uniformly, or heterogeneously — and can causal inference, specifically heterogeneous treatment effect (HTE) estimation, quantify who benefits, who is hurt, and through which mechanisms (champion composition, player skill, rest between games)?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Y_i(w)': 'Potential outcome for player i under treatment w', 'w_t, w_{t+1}': 'Consecutive patch versions', 'X_i': 'Match characteristics vector for player i', 'x_i': 'Realization of X_i'}
primitives.assumptions: Treatment assignment is as-if random; stable unit treatment value assumption (SUTVA); no interference between units.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When treatment effect varies significantly across subpopulations defined by match features.

layer2.mapping: Maps causal differences in win rates and performance metrics across player and team subgroups using recursive partitioning.
layer2.telemetry: Win rate change, KDA variation, champion pick frequency shifts

primitives.name: Causal Tree Partitioning
primitives.verbatim_quote: Trees greedily partition the feature space to **reduce the expected variance of the estimated HTE** (not CART loss), stopping at a predefined minimum leaf size or when no significant split remains.
primitives.assumptions: Feature space can be segmented to isolate distinct HTE patterns; splits are validated via t-test p-values.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When variance within leaves is minimized and statistical significance of splits is maintained.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to decision trees used in machine learning but optimized for causal variance reduction rather than predictive accuracy.
layer2.telemetry: Split significance (p-value), leaf size, variance reduction metric

primitives.name: Patch Impact Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Test bed: 62 League of Legends patches across 1.2M players, with outcomes at team level (win/loss) and player level (kills per match).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'Set of patches (62)', 'N': 'Number of players (1.2M)', 'T': 'Time period (mid-2014 to end of 2016)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each patch introduces a discrete treatment shift; outcomes are measurable at team and player levels.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When patch effects are detectable in aggregate behavior and individual performance metrics.

layer2.mapping: Analyzes temporal and compositional impact of patches on win rates and player stats using matched controls.
layer2.telemetry: Team win rate delta, kill count deviation, champion popularity trends

reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is the heterogeneous treatment effect (HTE) defined as τ(x_i) = E[Y_i(w_{t+1}) - Y_i(w_t) | X_i = x_i], where Y_i(w) represents the potential outcome under patch w for player i, and X_i denotes match-specific covariates. This formulation enables estimation of how different subpopulations respond differently to interventions. Causal trees optimize this by recursively splitting the feature space to minimize residual variance in estimated HTEs, using a validation set to generalize beyond training data. Each node’s estimate is a treated minus control mean difference with associated statistical significance. The methodology assumes that treatment assignment is effectively random, enabling causal inference through comparison of outcomes before and after patch application. Failure modes include omitted variable bias due to unmeasured confounders, violation of SUTVA, and insufficient sample sizes in leaf nodes leading to unstable estimates.
